Perfect Tenses

Every good cook knows two things: what they have already made — and when they made it. Today we learn the grammar behind both.

Kitchen Verbs

≈ 7 min
Talk Before we cook, let's talk. Answer out loud.

Look at the picture of the ingredients. Tell your teacher:

  • 🍳 What food can you see? Name five things.
  • 👨‍🍳 Have you ever cooked something with these? What was it?
  • 😋 What did you eat for breakfast today?
📝 Заметка для учителя▼
Разогрев на 3–4 минуты. Не исправляйте грамматику здесь — просто разговорите Ваню и посмотрите, тянет ли он уже have you ever cooked / what did you eat. Обратите внимание: третий вопрос специально в Past Simple (breakfast today = законченное конкретное время), а второй — в Present Perfect (опыт). Это тихо готовит контраст, который разберём в Step 2. Если отвечает односложно — попросите одну полную фразу.

How the Tenses Work

≈ 15 min

Ingredient 1 — Present Perfect

We use it for actions connected to now: life experience, news, or a result we can see. The exact time is unknown or not important.

I / You / We / Theyhave He / She / Ithas +past participle
Short forms: I've, he's, we've … · Negative: haven't / hasn't · Question: Have you…? / Has she…?

Tap the cards to see when we use it 👇

tap
Experience
Something in your life, any time before now.
Have you ever eaten sushi?
ever / never
Time is not important — only that it happened (or didn't) in your life.
I've never tried quinoa.
tap
Result now
A past action, but we care about the result we see now.
I've washed the tomatoes.
(they're clean now!)
We don't say when — the point is the tomatoes are ready.
He's made lunch. Let's eat!
tap
just / already
Finished a very short time ago, or sooner than expected.
I've just finished the sauce.
position
just / already go between have/has and the verb.
She's already baked a cake.
tap
yet
For things not done — in questions and negatives.
Have you chopped the onions yet?
position
yet goes at the end of the sentence.
I haven't served dessert yet.

Ingredient 2 — Past Simple (a quick reminder)

You already know this one. We use it for a finished action at a definite time in the past. We usually say when.

I / You / He / She / We / They+ verb + ed / irregular (ate, made, bought…)
Negative: didn't + verb · Question: Did you…? — I cooked · I didn't cook · Did you cook?

The secret: which one do I use?

This is the whole lesson in one place. Same action — cook dinner — two different tenses:

🍲 Present Perfect
Time is unknown / not important / "up to now"
  • Life experience: ever, never
  • Result we see now
  • Recently, so far, just, already, yet
"I've cooked dinner." → it's ready!
📅 Past Simple
There is a definite finished time
  • yesterday, last week, an hour ago
  • in 2020, when I was ten
  • We say (or ask) when
"I cooked dinner an hour ago." → when?
🧭
Golden rule for Vanya: if you can add a finished time word (yesterday, ago, in 2019) → Past Simple. If the time is unknown or you mean "in my life / up to now" → Present Perfect. Ask yourself: "When?" — if there's a clear answer, it's Past Simple.
📝 Заметка для учителя▼
Ключевой слайд урока. Дайте Ване проговорить пару своих примеров одной и той же ситуации в двух временах (напр. "I've done my homework" vs "I did my homework yesterday"). Частая ошибка на A2+ — тянуть Present Perfect с конкретным временем («I've cooked it yesterday»). Если услышите — не объясняйте заново, просто спросите «When?» и дайте самому исправить. «Золотое правило» специально сформулировано через вопрос When? — это рабочий якорь на все упражнения ниже.

Ex B In the kitchen: complete the dialogue with the Present Perfect form of the verbs.
Mum
Can you help me with the cooking, please? I 've washed (wash) the tomatoes. Can you chop them for a sauce?
Dan
Sure. What do you want me to do?
— one minute later —
Dan
OK. I (chop) them. What's next?
Mum
Grandma (bring) some strawberries from her garden for dessert. Can you wash them?
Dan
Of course. Mm, the strawberries smell lovely. We (not have) strawberries for a long time.
Mum
Oh no! Janet (not leave) any cream in the fridge! What can we have with the strawberries?
Dan
How about ice cream? We (serve) strawberries and ice cream before.
Mum
Good idea!

Ex G ★ The big one — Present Perfect or Past Simple? Use the signal word to decide.

First, sort the time words. Tap a chip to send it to Present Perfect → tap again for Past Simple.

Present Perfect
Past Simple
not sorted yet
ever yesterday just two hours ago never last week already in 2020 yet when I was six

Now write the verb in the correct tense. The yellow word is your clue.

1. I (cook) pasta yesterday.
2. (you / ever / try) sushi? ever
3. She (already / finish) her homework. already
4. We (eat) at that restaurant last week.
5. He (never / be) to London. never
6. They (make) a cake two hours ago.
7. I (just / wash) the dishes. just

📝 Заметка для учителя▼
Это упражнение — сердце запроса на контраст (в самих листах 6.2/6.3 его нет, добавлено под Ваню). Each sentence is unambiguous thanks to the signal word. Если ошибается — верните к «золотому правилу»: «Can you add a finished time? → Past Simple». Предложения 3, 5, 7 проверяют позицию already / never / just внутри Present Perfect — если ставит их не туда («He has been never»), это хорошая мини-цель на след. урок.

Your Turn to Talk

≈ 10 min
Speak Two truths, two lies. Say the sentences about you — but make two of them false!

Use the Present Perfect (have / haven't + participle). Your teacher will guess which two are lies. 🕵️

  • 1I ______ (do) tomorrow's homework.
  • 2I ______ (bring) a sweet snack to school today.
  • 3My mum ______ (put) a banana in my bag.
  • 4I ______ (eat) a packet of crisps today.
  • 5My dad ______ (buy) a new phone.
  • 6I ______ (try) sushi.
📝 Заметка для учителя▼
Индивидуальный формат: угадываете вы («I think you haven't tried sushi!»). После каждой угадайки просите Ваню подтвердить полной фразой: «Yes, I have» / «No, I haven't». Это оживляет монотонный дрилл и даёт естественные short answers из Ex E.
Ask & answer The tense bridge — answer, then add a Past Simple detail.

This is the trick that makes you sound fluent: answer with Present Perfect, then give the "when" in Past Simple.

Q1

Have you ever baked cookies?

Answer + say when you last did it.

"Yes, I have. I baked some last month."
Q2

Have you ever eaten quinoa?

If not — use never.

"No, I haven't. I've never eaten it."
Q3

Has your mum ever cooked spaghetti?

Say when / how it was.

"Yes, she has. She cooked it on Sunday."
Q4

Have you ever made fresh lemonade?

Add a detail in Past Simple.

"Yes! I made it in summer. It was sour."

🍝 Look at the pasta. Have you ever cooked pasta? Tell your teacher the whole story: did you make it yourself? When? Was it good?

final dish — free speaking

Tell me about a dish you've cooked

Put everything on one plate. Talk for one minute about food you have made in your life — and add the details of when and how in the Past Simple.

"I've cooked… / I've made…" "I made it when…" "I've never cooked…, but I want to try." "Last time, I…"
📝 Заметка для учителя▼
Финальная продукция (2–3 мин). Слушайте на переключение времён: Present Perfect для факта/опыта («I've made pancakes») и Past Simple для деталей («I made them last Saturday. I burned the first one!»). Не перебивайте — соберите 2–3 ошибки и дайте фидбэк после, а не по ходу. Если время осталось — попросите Ваню задать вам три «Have you ever…?» вопроса.

Well done, chef! 🎉

You can now use two tenses like a pro: Present Perfect for experience and results, Past Simple for finished times.

The proof of the pudding is in the eating — now go and use it!
